messages:
Anya (PM): Hey team — I pushed an initial RFC draft for the Optimize toolkit (batching / caching / quantization) and want to lock down launch criteria and a minimal scope we can ship in Q2. Link: https://go.redwood/rfcs/optimize-toolkit-draft :paperclip:
optimize-bot: RFC created by Anya — https://go.redwood/rfcs/optimize-toolkit-draft (comments open)
Mike (ML Eng): skimmed it. major tech items: continuous batching + KV prefix cache + a tiered quantization recommendation matrix. need to call out expected perf gains per model family (gpt-like, llama-like).
Jess (Infra): rollout concerns: we must support hosted + dedicated + private. Private deploys can't assume HSM for keys; also cache invalidation signals differ across networks.
Samir (DevEx): docs + SDK surface: we should expose an optRecs endpoint that returns recommended batch_size, cache_policy, quant_profile per route. DevEx will own SDK ergonomic layer.
Anya (PM): Proposed minimal launch scope: 1) recommend batch sizes and batching policy suggestions 2) prefix KV caching with TTLs + telemetry 3) a single quantization recommendation (int8) with clear caveats. Launch criteria below — please comment with +1/concerns.
Mike (ML Eng): Acceptance criteria suggestion: - avg latency reduction >= 15% for text-gen p95 on baseline workloads OR token-cost reduction >= 20% for batchy workloads - no more than 1% regression in quality as measured by our eval suite (prompt set A) - end-to-end compatibility for streaming responses - fallbacks to non-quantized models if hallucination/regression detected
Jess (Infra): Add infra SLOs: - cache hit parity >= 70% for targeted prefixes in canary - no increase in tail CPU usage > 10% on control plane - autoscaler integration tested on Dedicated pools
Samir (DevEx): Docs/SDK gating: - example integration in JS/py + migration guide - one tutorial notebook for developers - an optRecs API swagger and sample responses
Anya (PM): Edge cases we should capture in PRD: variable sequence lengths, multi-tenant cache poisoning, encrypted payloads (can't cache), quantization-induced tokenization shifts, interactions with function calling.
Mike (ML Eng): On quantization: need a small regression harness per model that runs a 1000-sample eval comparing logits/topk and summary metrics (perplexity/ROUGE/whatever). If delta > threshold, mark "do not recommend". Also call out nondeterminism: seed/FP routes and fallback decisions.
Jess (Infra): Canary plan: - stage on a single region Hosted cluster + one Dedicated customer pool - collect 72h of telemetry (latency, cost per token, cache hit rate, error rate) - abort if p95 regressions > 10% or errors spike > 2x
Samir (DevEx): UX for recommendations: prefer a graded rec (e.g., "Safe: | Moderate: | Aggressive:") with estimated CPU/GPU savings. That reduces risk for ops teams.
Anya (PM): Draft launch checklist (short): - RFC + PRD approved - harness tests + regression alarm thresholds - SDK + docs + example - canary + abort policy - post-launch monitoring dashboard (cost/latency/quality)
Mike (ML Eng): Quick config example for the optRecs response (for SDK folks):
```json
{
  "model_family": "llama-2",
  "safe": {"batch_size": "8", "cache_policy": "prefix-ttl-30s", "quant": "none"},
  "moderate": {"batch_size": "16", "cache_policy": "prefix-ttl-60s", "quant": "int8-llama"},
  "aggressive": {"batch_size": "32", "cache_policy": "prefix-ttl-120s", "quant": "int8-llama-aggr"}
}
```
Samir (DevEx): That looks good. We'll need example pseudocode for SDK: how to apply suggestions and a safe fallback wrapper.
Jess (Infra): Ops note: cache TTLs can't be global — expose per-customer override and a namespace isolation flag. Also evictions must be observable.
Anya (PM): Customer-driven asks to incorporate: - enterprise customers want opt-out per route + audit logs - a KPI export for finance (cost saved) - regression alerting to signal product managers when quality drops
Mike (ML Eng): Prioritization ask: I'd like to split into phases: Phase 1 (MVP): batch recs + simple prefix cache + telemetry. Phase 2: quant recs + regression harness + SDK automation. Phase 3: auto-tuning and RL-backed recommendations.
Samir (DevEx): Timeline: we can ship Phase 1 docs + SDK changes in ~6 weeks if eng + infra align. Need 2 engineers full-time for 4 weeks to implement backend rec engine + telemetry hooks.
Anya (PM): Okay — can we get owners? @Mike to own Phase1 engine, @Jess infra can own canary/observability, @Samir owns SDK/docs. I'll consolidate into PRD and share for formal approvals by Fri. :calendar: 
Mike (ML Eng): I can slot engineers: Alex and Priya. Alex on batching engine, Priya on telemetry hooks.
Jess (Infra): I'll schedule infra tests and allocate a Dedicated pool for canary.
Samir (DevEx): I'll draft SDK + migration guide. Will post a PR by Tue.
Anya (PM): Great — thanks. Please add comments on the RFC doc with concrete numbers for model families. Low-verbosity thumbs: +1 or -1.
Mike (ML Eng): +1
Jess (Infra): +1
Samir (DevEx): +1
optimize-bot: Reminder — RFC comment window closes in 72 hours.
